notes.mark_coverage: mark-price klines are used where the cached mark archive has a bar; the perp 1h high/low stand in before a symbol's first mark bar and for holes after it (last-price wicks are usually wider than mark wicks, so this errs toward more liquidations).  The real first mark bar per symbol, the fallback bar counts and the number of episodes with fallback or missing hours are recorded in the output, not asserted here
notes.simulation: sleeve-level simulation on the canonical 8h equity_path intervals (leverage_sim's per-position booking at entry breaks the daily bootstrap for multi-day holds): per sleeve, episodes occupy disjoint intervals [entry, exit); levered interval return = unlevered x L floored at -100%; each episode is checked for liquidation from the entry fill with the running adverse excursion over mark bars in (entry, exit]; on liquidation at 8h interval tau that episode's own intervals from entry through tau are replaced by one loss |w|(1 + 0.005 L) of the sleeve capital at entry, its remaining intervals up to the scheduled exit are 0 and its exit cost and last funding settlement are removed from the exit interval (shared with the next episode's entry when the position flips); other episodes are never touched; intervals are then compounded to the 00:00 daily stamps and averaged over sleeves
notes.max_safe_leverage: headline = largest L with P(ruin 365d) <= 5% in BOTH samples (whole and 2023-2026) and zero liquidations in the 2023-2026 path (stricter reading); per-sample values also reported
notes.windows: daily stamp d covers day d-1 (repo convention); annual return = final_equity^(365/days) - 1; each sample slices the full-history path and bootstraps from the slice
notes.funding: funding is checked per sleeve before any statistic: for every episode (entry bar i, exit bar j) each bar open i+1..j (the position is held into that open, terminal bar included) must have its funding settlements in (previous open, this open] (canonical align_funding slots); the expected number per bar follows the symbol's own funding interval derived from the settlement gaps (8h -> 1, 4h -> 2, 1h -> 8; gaps median-smoothed over 7 neighbours). Holes while the sleeve is flat do not fail. REST verification (added 2026-10-12, after the first launch of the single run stopped at this check before any statistic and wrote no output: ENAUSDT 4h funding, no 04:00 settlement on 2026-06-24 in the archive): for every held bar flagged as short, the public Binance REST endpoint GET /fapi/v1/fundingRate (no key) is queried for (previous open, this open]. Settlements REST has and the archive lacks are merged into the funding series (the sleeve is rerun with them); a bar where REST returns what the archive has (at least one settlement) is accepted as exchange-confirmed (the exchange skipped that settlement), and the bar is booked with the settlements that exist; a bar with zero settlements still needs REST to return at least one. A REST error, an unparseable answer, or an empty REST answer for a short bar fails the run, and so does a short bar when no REST client is configured. The bars confirmed by REST (with times and counts) and the settlements repaired from REST (times and rates) are recorded per symbol in the output provenance (funding_rest_verification)
notes.revision: 2026-10-12, before the single run: liquidation bookkeeping rebuilt on 8h intervals after review (an earlier daily-granular version mixed episodes of one sleeve)
notes.data_integrity: loaded perp and mark high/low must be finite, positive and ordered, otherwise the run fails (a NaN would silently block later liquidations); provenance records per symbol the largest relative |mark - perp| at matching hourly bars and the 10 largest episode adverse excursions, to expose bad mark wicks (descriptive)
